name: WHO Editorial Style
description: Editorial conventions from the WHO Editorial Style Guide. Governs British English spelling, WHO-specific punctuation, people-first terminology, NLM/Vancouver citation style, and WHO country/territory naming conventions. Applies to all narrative content in WHO-affiliated folios.

rules.name: British English spelling
rules.description: Use British English spelling as the baseline for all WHO publications. Use -ise/-isation (not -ize/-ization). Use 'programme' (not 'program' unless referring to computer programs). Use 'centre' (not 'center'). Use 'behaviour' (not 'behavior'). Use 'colour' (not 'color'). Use 'defence' (not 'defense'). Use 'licence' (noun), 'license' (verb).

terminology.context: Unless referring to a computer program

rules.name: No periods after courtesy titles
rules.description: Do not use periods after courtesy titles: Dr (not Dr.), Mr (not Mr.), Ms (not Ms.), Mrs (not Mrs.), Prof (not Prof.).

patterns.message: WHO style: no period after courtesy titles (Dr not Dr., Mr not Mr.)

rules.name: People-first language
rules.description: Use respectful, people-first language. Say 'person living with HIV' (not 'HIV patient' or 'AIDS victim'). Say 'person with diabetes' (not 'diabetic'). Say 'person with a disability' (not 'disabled person' or 'handicapped'). Say 'older person' (not 'the elderly'). Say 'child/person who is malnourished' (not 'malnourished child'). Avoid labelling people by their condition.

terminology.context: People-first: do not define people by their condition

rules.name: NLM/Vancouver citation style
rules.description: References follow the NLM (National Library of Medicine) / Vancouver citation style. Include DOIs, PMIDs, and PMCIDs where available. Author names: surname followed by initials without periods or spaces (e.g. 'Smith AB'). Journal titles abbreviated per NLM standards. List up to 6 authors; after 6 use 'et al.'.

rules.name: WHO Member State naming
rules.description: Use official WHO Member State short names in running text. Use the full formal name only in legal/treaty contexts. Never use colloquial or outdated country names. Refer to the WHO list of Member States for official names. Some key examples: 'Republic of Korea' (not 'South Korea'), 'Democratic People's Republic of Korea' (not 'North Korea'), 'Côte d'Ivoire' (not 'Ivory Coast'), 'Türkiye' (not 'Turkey'), 'Czechia' (not 'Czech Republic').

rules.name: Abbreviation conventions
rules.description: Spell out abbreviations at first use, followed by the abbreviation in parentheses. Exception: universally known abbreviations (WHO, UN, HIV, AIDS, DNA, RNA) need not be spelled out. Use no periods in abbreviations (WHO not W.H.O.). Avoid starting sentences with abbreviations.

rules.name: Number formatting
rules.description: Spell out numbers one through nine in running text; use figures for 10 and above. Use a space (not a comma) as a thousands separator in numbers ≥ 10 000. Use a period as the decimal marker. In tables and figures, use figures throughout. Percentages: use the % symbol with a figure (25%), not 'percent' or 'per cent'.

rules.name: Date formatting
rules.description: Use day month year format without commas or ordinal suffixes: '15 March 2024' (not 'March 15, 2024' or '15th March 2024'). Months may be abbreviated in tables: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec.

rules.name: Gender-inclusive language
rules.description: Use gender-inclusive language throughout. Avoid 'he' as a generic pronoun; use 'they' or restructure. Say 'chairperson' (not 'chairman'), 'workforce' or 'staff' (not 'manpower'), 'artificial' or 'synthetic' (not 'man-made'). Specify sex or gender only when relevant to the content.

rules.name: No serial (Oxford) comma
rules.description: WHO style does not use the serial (Oxford) comma before 'and'/'or' in simple lists. Write 'apples, oranges and bananas' (not 'apples, oranges, and bananas'). Exception: use a comma before 'and'/'or' when needed for clarity in complex lists.
